value.body: A doctor who diagnoses and treats common illnesses, manages long-term conditions such as diabetes and hypertension, and refers patients to specialists when needed. General physicians work in government health centres and hospitals, private clinics and hospitals, and in their own practice. With an MBBS, doctors work as general practitioners or medical officers; hospital "physician" posts usually mean an MD in General Medicine.

items.label: Course length (MBBS)
items.note: 4.5 years of study plus a 1-year compulsory rotating internship

items.label: Registration
items.value: National Medical Commission or a State Medical Council

items.label: Registered allopathic doctors
items.note: Registered with State Medical Councils and NMC; not all are active
items.source: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare reply in Parliament (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Entry is through NEET-UG for an MBBS seat, followed by the internship and registration with the NMC or a State Medical Council. After that, a doctor can work as a medical officer or general practitioner. A national exit test (NExT) has been proposed as a common final-year and licensing exam; its rollout timeline has changed more than once.

value.title: At a glance
items: Many doctors go on to a postgraduate degree (MD, MS or DNB) through NEET-PG.
Government service, including rural postings, is a common first job.
Long hours and night duties are common in the early years.
